title: 14 remaining EXP-301/EXP-302 effects_subsystem_test blocks fail; transition() emits no effect_emitted for SERVICE_TASK
symptom: After ISS-0149 made tests/integration/effects_subsystem_test.zig compile for the first time and fixed 16 of its 30 failing blocks, 14 blocks still fail. The largest cluster is TC-EXP-302-02/03/04/06/07/08, which all panic with `index out of bounds: index 0, len 0` at `result.emitted_events[0]` — transition() returns ZERO emitted events when a token enters a SERVICE_TASK node, so the EXP-302 async-effect emission path produces nothing to assert on. TC-EXP-302-01 and TC-EXP-302-05 fail/leak against the same path. TC-EXP-301-05/07/08/09/11/12 fail or leak individually on the worker sweep and re-entry paths.
root_cause: PREMISE CORRECTED. transition() DOES emit effect_emitted for SERVICE_TASK and always did - the "zero emitted events" symptom was the dangling-graph fixture bug (makeServiceTaskGraph took attrs as a runtime parameter, demoting the node array from static to stack memory), already fixed under GH #439/#490 commit 8103072 before this run. The 13 remaining failures were FIVE independent memory-ownership defects: (RC-1) EffectEmittedPayload.kind aliased a static string literal while its four sibling fields were allocator-owned, so uniform freeing segfaulted on read-only .rdata; (RC-2) src/effects/worker.zig deliverSpec never freed parseHttpEffectSpec/parseEmailEffectSpec results - a live production leak of 2-5 allocations per delivery; (RC-3) reenterEffectResult omitted the NOT NULL events.sequence_number column, so EVERY effect re-entry failed with PostgreSQL C23502 - the async effects loop could never close in production; (RC-4) four leaks in transition.zig on paths that discard state (putVariableSafe key orphaning, borrowed response body stored as owned, .effect_failed dropped token+array, .END freed discarded tokens only when completing); (RC-5) the test file kept drifted hand-copies of freeInstanceState/freeTransitionResult that under-freed.
reproduction:
1. docker-compose db_test healthy, BPM_TEST_DB_URL set.
2. zig build test-integration-svc
3. Observe 14 `error: 'effects_subsystem_test.test.TC-EXP-30*'` lines.
impact: EXP-301 (async effects outbox) and EXP-302 (SERVICE_TASK migration to async effects) are marked implemented but their integration tests have never passed. If TC-EXP-302's reading is correct, SERVICE_TASK nodes do not emit effects at all, meaning the async service-task path is non-functional in production, not merely untested.
candidate_resolution: Start with TC-EXP-302-02: read src/engine/transition.zig's processNodeEntry SERVICE_TASK branch against the EXP-302 requirement and determine whether effect_emitted is supposed to be produced there. That single answer decides whether the six TC-EXP-302 failures are a production defect or six wrong tests. Treat the six TC-EXP-301 failures separately — they are individual worker/re-entry assertions, not one cluster.
notes: Filed rather than fixed inline because ISS-0149's scope is the ten specific integration files named in GH #465, all ten of which now pass in isolation. effects_subsystem_test.zig is NOT one of them; it entered the picture only because GH #439's wiring commit made it a compile-blocker for the whole test-integration umbrella, which ISS-0149 had to clear to see any results at all. The compile fixes, the missing-migration fix, and 16 of the 30 failures were resolved under ISS-0149 as unavoidable unblocking work; the remaining 14 require a production-behaviour decision about EXP-302 that is properly its own diagnosis.
resolution: Fixed all five root causes in source (no assertions weakened, no tests skipped). effects_subsystem_test failing blocks 13 -> 3; whole suite 90 fail/9 crash -> 88 fail/2 crash with ZERO regressions (diffed full sorted failure-name sets). zig build test exits 0. src/engine/transition.zig remains I/O-free. The 3 survivors are distinct root causes forwarded as ISS-0186/#520, ISS-0187/#521, ISS-0188/#522. GH #515 (ISS-0182) was a duplicate of this issue and was closed and de-queued.
prevention: A struct crossing a module boundary must have uniform field ownership - a single borrowed field among owned ones is unfreeable by any caller. Test files must not hand-copy engine teardown helpers; transition.zig exports freeInstanceState and freeTransitionResult as pub precisely so they cannot drift.
